claims.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy distinguishes poor academic practice from academic misconduct: an ASB Chair may decide a concern is an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice (for example incomplete citation), which is not misconduct; the student receives feedback and the work is marked against the criteria. Blatant, extensive or careless failures are excluded from this category.

evidence.quote: Once the ASB Chair (or their nominee) has reviewed the information available, they may decide that the concern relates to poor academic practice and that no academic misconduct has occurred. additionalTopics.summary: King's College London supports considered use of generative AI and is open to evolving teaching, assessment, and feedback practices according to need and disciplinary differences. Institutional guidance for AI-assisted marking and feedback (July 2025) emphasizes that reading and assessing student work should primarily be conducted by humans, with human oversight essential to ensure accuracy and appropriateness. Staff should not use GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI, as these tools are notoriously unreliable. Staff should never upload student work or include student details into any AI system or GenAI tool without explicit consent, permission, and forethought; approved or supported university GenAI tools should be used for AI-assisted feedback and marking. This guidance governs staff marking and data handling, and does not set course permissions for students.

claims.claimText: King's Academic Misconduct Policy distinguishes poor academic practice from academic misconduct: an ASB Chair may decide a concern is an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice (for example incomplete citation), which is not misconduct; the student receives feedback and the work is marked against the criteria. Blatant, extensive or careless failures are excluded from this category.

It does not include when the failure to adhere to scholarly practice is blatant, extensive or results from a lack of effort. Poor academic practice is not a form of academic misconduct.

claims.claimText: Under King's Academic Misconduct Policy, a suspected case normally goes first to a Stage One Academic Integrity Meeting (AIM) with two staff members. The AIM is not a hearing and should be informal, supportive and exploratory; where authorship or third-party involvement is in doubt the student may be asked to explain their answers, ideas or references, but must not be pressured or obliged to give specific responses and may respond in writing instead. Staff share their notes, and the student may add information, normally within 5 working days. Possible Stage One outcomes are no concern, poor academic practice, a local educative or restorative outcome, or referral to a Stage Two Misconduct Committee.

Where a Stage One AIM finds misconduct and applies a local penalty (Outcome 3), the student may send a contestation in writing to Student Conduct & Appeals within 10 working days from the date of written notification of the Stage One outcome. Possible outcomes range from educative measures such as a formal warning or capped resubmission to punitive outcomes up to suspension or expulsion; AI use does not carry an automatic penalty.

Copying AI output into a submission is not appropriate under the Academic Misconduct Policy, and work must remain the student's own; ask if unsure.

disclosure.en: Students must acknowledge any generative AI use in coursework with a declaration statement alongside the references, unless the assessment brief gives other wording: either that no part was generated by AI (grammar and spell checking is consistent with this) or that parts have AI contributions within the brief's acceptable use, naming the tools and how they were used. AI is not cited as an authoritative source. Doctoral students choose one of two AI declarations on the RD2 form.
disclosure.zh: 学生须在课程作业的参考文献处附声明，说明生成式 AI 的使用情况（考核说明另有措辞的除外）：要么声明没有任何部分由 AI 生成（使用语法和拼写检查与此一致），要么声明部分内容有 AI 参与且符合考核说明的可接受范围，并写明工具及用途。AI 不作为权威来源引用。博士生须在 RD2 表格中选择两种 AI 声明之一。

privacy_data.en: Students should not input personal data, sensitive information or content created by others into any AI platform, even though King's Copilot has commercial data protection. Doctoral students must discuss confidentiality, copyright, data protection and ethics with their supervisors and get written approval before uploading any part of their research. Staff must not upload student work or details to AI tools without explicit permission.
privacy_data.zh: 即使国王学院的 Copilot 有商业数据保护，学生也不应向任何 AI 平台输入个人数据、敏感信息或他人创作的内容。博士生在上传研究项目任何部分前，须与导师团队讨论保密、版权、数据保护和伦理问题并取得书面批准。教职员工未经明确许可不得把学生作品或信息上传到 AI 工具。

approved_tools.en: All King's students and staff can use Microsoft Copilot text and image generation by signing in with their KCL Microsoft account; the Enterprise licence provides commercial data protection. King's does not describe Copilot as the only or required tool, and access does not authorise its use in a particular assessment.
approved_tools.zh: 国王学院全体学生和员工可用 KCL 微软账号登录使用 Microsoft Copilot 的文本和图像生成；企业许可提供商业数据保护。学校并未把 Copilot 描述为唯一或必须使用的工具，能使用也不代表获准在某项考核中使用。

research_publication.en: Doctoral students may use AI in an assistive role to clarify their own writing, including rewriting or paraphrasing parts of the thesis, but not to replace their authorship; AI in the research process itself (e.g. data analysis) falls under research design and ethics review. Uploading research material needs prior written supervisory approval, theses carry an RD2 AI declaration, and examiners must not upload theses to AI or use AI detectors.
research_publication.zh: 博士生可将 AI 作为辅助工具澄清自己的写作，包括改写或意译论文部分内容，但不能替代本人的作者身份；研究过程中的 AI（如数据分析）属于研究设计和伦理审查范畴。上传研究材料须事先取得导师团队书面批准，论文须附 RD2 AI 声明，评审人不得把论文上传到 AI 或使用 AI 检测工具。

academic_integrity.en: Inappropriate, unattributed AI use can be academic misconduct, but poor academic practice (e.g. incomplete citation) is not misconduct. Cases normally start with an informal Academic Integrity Meeting where students may be asked to explain their work but need not give specific answers. A Stage One penalty can be contested within 10 working days of written notification; a Misconduct Committee decision can be appealed within 10 working days on limited grounds. Outcomes range from warnings and capped resubmission to suspension or expulsion. King's has not enabled Turnitin's AI-detection percentage, though similarity checking continues.
academic_integrity.zh: 不当且未注明的 AI 使用可构成学术不端，但不规范的学术做法（如引用不完整）不属于不端。案件通常从非正式的学术诚信会议开始，学生可能被要求解释作品，但无义务给出特定回答。第一阶段处罚可在书面通知后 10 个工作日内提出异议；不端委员会决定可在 10 个工作日内基于有限理由上诉。处理结果从警告、限分重交到停学或开除不等。国王学院未启用 Turnitin 的 AI 检测百分比，但相似性检查仍在使用。

teaching_guidance.en: King's College London supports considered use of generative AI and is open to evolving teaching, assessment, and feedback practices according to need and disciplinary differences. Institutional guidance for AI-assisted marking and feedback (July 2025) emphasizes that reading and assessing student work should primarily be conducted by humans, with human oversight essential to ensure accuracy and appropriateness. Staff should not use GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI, as these tools are notoriously unreliable. Staff should never upload student work or include student details into any AI system or GenAI tool without explicit consent, permission, and forethought; approved or supported university GenAI tools should be used for AI-assisted feedback and marking. This guidance governs staff marking and data handling, and does not set course permissions for students.
teaching_guidance.zh: 伦敦国王学院支持审慎使用生成式 AI，并愿意根据需求和学科差异改进教学、考核与反馈实践。关于 AI 辅助评分与反馈的机构指引（2025年7月）强调，审阅和评估学生作业应主要由人工进行，且必须有人工监督以确保准确性和适切性。教师不应使用 GenAI 工具来检测学生的 AI 使用情况，因为此类工具极不可靠。未经明确同意、许可与深思熟虑，工作人员绝不应将学生作业或个人信息上传至任何 AI 系统或 GenAI 工具；进行 AI 辅助反馈和评分时，应使用学校批准或支持的大学 GenAI 工具。该指引规范教职人员的评分与数据处理实践，并非针对学生的课程使用许可。

privacy_data.en: Students should not input personal data, sensitive information or content created by others into any AI platform, even though King's Copilot has commercial data protection. Doctoral students must discuss confidentiality, copyright, data protection and ethics with their supervisors and get written approval before uploading any part of their research. Staff must not upload student work or details to AI tools without explicit permission.

research_publication.en: Doctoral students may use AI in an assistive role to clarify their own writing, including rewriting or paraphrasing parts of the thesis, but not to replace their authorship; AI in the research process itself (e.g. data analysis) falls under research design and ethics review. Uploading research material needs prior written supervisory approval, theses carry an RD2 AI declaration, and examiners must not upload theses to AI or use AI detectors.

academic_integrity.en: Inappropriate, unattributed AI use can be academic misconduct, but poor academic practice (e.g. incomplete citation) is not misconduct. Cases normally start with an informal Academic Integrity Meeting where students may be asked to explain their work but need not give specific answers. A Stage One penalty can be contested within 10 working days of written notification; a Misconduct Committee decision can be appealed within 10 working days on limited grounds. Outcomes range from warnings and capped resubmission to suspension or expulsion. King's has not enabled Turnitin's AI-detection percentage, though similarity checking continues.
academic_integrity.zh: 不当且未注明的 AI 使用可构成学术不端，但不规范的学术做法（如引用不完整）不属于不端。案件通常从非正式的学术诚信会议开始，学生可能被要求解释作品，但无义务给出特定回答。第一阶段处罚可在书面通知后 10 个工作日内提出异议；不端委员会决定可在 10 个工作日内基于有限理由上诉。处理结果从警告、限分重交到停学或开除不等。国王学院未启用 Turnitin 的 AI 检测百分比，但相似性检查仍在使用。

teaching_guidance.en: King's College London supports considered use of generative AI and is open to evolving teaching, assessment, and feedback practices according to need and disciplinary differences. Institutional guidance for AI-assisted marking and feedback (July 2025) emphasizes that reading and assessing student work should primarily be conducted by humans, with human oversight essential to ensure accuracy and appropriateness. Staff should not use GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI, as these tools are notoriously unreliable. Staff should never upload student work or include student details into any AI system or GenAI tool without explicit consent, permission, and forethought; approved or supported university GenAI tools should be used for AI-assisted feedback and marking. This guidance governs staff marking and data handling, and does not set course permissions for students.

Where a Stage One AIM finds misconduct and applies a local penalty (Outcome 3), the student may send a contestation in writing to Student Conduct & Appeals within 10 working days from the date of written notification of the Stage One outcome. A Stage Two Misconduct Committee decision may be appealed, on the grounds of new evidence or significant procedural error, by submitting a Misconduct Appeal Form within 10 working days of the date of the Misconduct Committee outcome. Possible outcomes range from educative measures such as a formal warning or capped resubmission to punitive outcomes up to suspension or expulsion; AI use does not carry an automatic penalty.

draft-claim-kcl-poor-academic-practice.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy distinguishes poor academic practice from academic misconduct: an ASB Chair may decide a concern is an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice (for example incomplete citation), which is not misconduct; the student receives feedback and the work is marked against the criteria. Blatant, extensive or careless failures are excluded from this category.

evidence.quote: Once the ASB Chair (or their nominee) has reviewed the information available, they may decide that the concern relates to poor academic practice and that no academic misconduct has occurred. Poor academic practice involves an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice. Examples include when sources are acknowledged to some extent, but citation is inadequate or incomplete. It does not include when the failure to adhere to scholarly practice is blatant, extensive or results from a lack of effort. Poor academic practice is not a form of academic misconduct.
